source: Index Librorum Prohibitorum (Roman, 1559-1948), with notes from Spanish/Portuguese indices and other suppressions where relevant
notes: Curated for overlap with Source Library's domain (Hermetica, alchemy, Kabbalah, Rosicrucianism, magic, astrology, Renaissance/early-modern philosophy and theology). Not exhaustive — focuses on authors and works whose suppression is well-attested in standard scholarship (Reusch, Bujanda, De Bujanda's 'Index des livres interdits' 1985-2002). Date fields refer to FIRST placement on a Roman Index unless noted.

entries.author: Giordano Bruno
entries.index: Roman 1603; carried forward in all subsequent editions through 1948
entries.notes: Opera omnia condemned 1603; executed by Roman Inquisition 17 Feb 1600 in Campo de' Fiori. Major Hermetic works: De umbris idearum, De la causa, Spaccio de la bestia trionfante, Eroici furori.

entries.author: Tommaso Campanella
entries.index: Roman 1633 (De sensu rerum); subsequent additions
entries.notes: Dominican philosopher; spent 27 years in Neapolitan prisons. Hermetic-magical cosmology drawn from Telesio and Ficino.

entries.author: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa
entries.index: Roman 1559 (Paul IV); reaffirmed all editions
entries.notes: Foundational Renaissance synthesis of natural magic, Kabbalah, and Hermeticism. Source Library's De occulta philosophia is canonical.

entries.author: Marsilio Ficino
works: De vita libri tres (especially De vita coelitus comparanda)
entries.index: Investigated 1489 by Innocent VIII for astral magic in De vita III; Ficino's apology accepted, but later editions appeared on local indices.
entries.notes: Translator of Corpus Hermeticum, Plato, Plotinus. De vita coelitus comparanda is the foundational text of Renaissance astral/talismanic magic.

entries.author: Pietro Pomponazzi
entries.index: Roman 1559; De incantationibus suppressed before publication, printed posthumously 1556.
entries.notes: Paduan Averroist; denied natural-reason proof of soul's immortality. De incantationibus offers naturalistic explanation of miracles.

entries.author: Paracelsus
entries.index: Various works on Roman Index 1559 onward; theological works particularly suppressed.
entries.notes: Foundational figure of iatrochemistry. Many works circulated only in MS or pseudonymous editions due to censorship.

entries.author: Robert Fludd
works: Utriusque cosmi maioris scilicet et minoris... historia
entries.index: Roman 1631 (decree against Fludd's works generally); attacked by Mersenne and Gassendi.
entries.notes: English Paracelsian; engravings by Merian. Macrocosm-microcosm synthesis of Hermetic, Kabbalistic, Rosicrucian thought.

entries.author: Johannes Trithemius
entries.index: Roman 1609 (Steganographia); other works (Polygraphia, De septem secundeis) generally tolerated.
entries.notes: Benedictine abbot of Sponheim. Steganographia uses angelic invocations as cryptographic cover — became a foundational text of early-modern angel magic.

entries.author: Heinrich Khunrath
entries.index: Condemned by Sorbonne 1625; placed on Roman Index in subsequent editions.
entries.notes: Foundational alchemical-Kabbalistic synthesis; the laboratory-oratory engraving is canonical Western esoteric iconography.

entries.author: Pico della Mirandola, Giovanni
entries.index: 13 theses condemned by Innocent VIII 1487; Apologia (1487) also condemned. Pico imprisoned briefly; rehabilitated by Alexander VI 1493.
entries.notes: First Christian Kabbalist; introduced Kabbalah to Latin West. Oratio de hominis dignitate is the prologue to the Conclusiones.

entries.author: Pico della Mirandola, Gianfrancesco
entries.index: Some works on Roman Index 1559; selectively expurgated.
entries.notes: Nephew of Giovanni Pico; major theorist of demonology and critic of astrology.

entries.author: Pietro d'Abano
entries.index: Roman 1559; works on astrology and natural magic suppressed.
entries.notes: Paduan philosopher-physician; tried for heresy. The Heptameron of ritual magic is attributed pseudonymously.

entries.author: Cecco d'Ascoli
entries.index: Burned 1327 with the author (Florence); placed on Roman Index 1559.
entries.notes: Astrologer-poet; executed for heresy in Florence. His commentary on Sacrobosco's Sphaera was also suppressed.

entries.author: Roger Bacon
works: De secretis operibus artis et naturae
entries.index: Alchemical works on Roman Index 1559; pseudo-Baconian alchemy widely circulated.
entries.notes: Franciscan; allegedly imprisoned by his order for suspect studies.

entries.author: Ramon Llull
entries.index: Pseudo-Lullian alchemical works on Roman Index 1559; Llull's authentic works defended by Spain.
entries.notes: The vast pseudo-Lullian alchemical corpus (Testamentum, etc.) is distinct from the genuine philosophical works.

entries.author: Galileo Galilei
works: Dialogo sopra i due massimi sistemi del mondo
entries.index: Dialogo banned 1633 by Holy Office; remained on Index until 1758 (general decree) and explicitly until 1835.
entries.notes: Convicted of suspicion of heresy 1633; held under house arrest until death 1642.

entries.author: Nicolaus Copernicus
entries.index: Suspended donec corrigatur 1616; explicit corrections issued 1620; removed from Index 1758.
entries.notes: Only 10 sentences required correction in the 1620 expurgation — but the suspension shaped a century of suppressed cosmology.

entries.author: Johannes Kepler
entries.index: Epitome on Roman Index 1619 (with Copernicus suspension); Kepler's Harmonices Mundi escaped formal condemnation but was suspect.
entries.notes: Lutheran astronomer; mother tried for witchcraft 1620. Harmonice mundi grounds astronomy in Pythagorean number-mysticism.

entries.author: Niccolò Machiavelli
works: Discorsi sopra la prima deca di Tito Livio
entries.index: Opera omnia, Roman 1559 (Paul IV); reaffirmed in all subsequent editions.
entries.notes: All works condemned; published in Protestant cities throughout the suppression.

entries.author: Desiderius Erasmus
entries.index: Roman 1559 (Paul IV) listed Erasmus among Class I auctores damnati (all works prohibited); Trent (1564) moved most works to second-class (donec corrigatur).
entries.notes: Most prominent humanist on the Pauline Index. Selectively expurgated under Trent.

entries.author: Martin Luther
entries.index: Condemned by Leo X bull Decet Romanum Pontificem 1521; reaffirmed Roman 1559 and every subsequent edition.
entries.notes: Class I auctor damnatus.

entries.author: John Calvin
entries.index: Roman 1559; Class I auctor damnatus.

entries.author: Michael Servetus
entries.index: Roman 1559; works also condemned by Calvin's Geneva (Servetus burned there 1553).
entries.notes: Burned at Geneva 1553 by Calvin's authorities. Christianismi Restitutio — only 3 copies survived. Discovered pulmonary circulation.

entries.author: Sebastian Castellio
entries.index: Roman 1559.
entries.notes: Tolerationist; opposed Calvin over execution of Servetus.

entries.author: Faustus Socinus
entries.index: Roman 1603; Racovian Catechism (1605) condemned by all confessions.
entries.notes: Foundational Antitrinitarian; Polish Brethren.

entries.author: Baruch Spinoza
entries.index: Tractatus on Roman Index 1679; Opera posthuma 1690. Also cherem (excommunication) by Amsterdam Jewish community 1656.
entries.notes: Excommunicated by Amsterdam 1656 at age 23.

entries.author: Thomas Hobbes
entries.index: De cive on Roman Index 1654; Leviathan added; Opera latina condemned 1703. Leviathan also burned at Oxford 1683.

entries.author: René Descartes
entries.index: Opera donec corrigantur, Roman 1663.

entries.author: Blaise Pascal
entries.index: Lettres provinciales on Roman Index 1657 (also burned at Aix-en-Provence); Pensées partially suspect.

entries.author: Pierre Bayle
entries.index: Dictionnaire on Roman Index 1701.

entries.author: John Locke
entries.index: Essay on Roman Index 1734.

entries.author: Voltaire
entries.index: Most works on Roman Index from 1752; opera omnia eventually condemned. Many works also publicly burned in Paris.

entries.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
entries.index: Émile and Contrat social on Roman Index 1762; burned at Paris 1762.

entries.author: Denis Diderot
entries.index: Pensées 1751; Encyclopédie on Roman Index 1759; Lettre sur les aveugles led to brief imprisonment 1749.

entries.author: David Hume
entries.index: Opera on Roman Index 1761.

entries.author: Immanuel Kant
entries.index: Critique of Pure Reason on Roman Index 1827.

entries.author: Giovanni Boccaccio
entries.index: Decameron on Roman 1559; expurgated edition (Salviati) permitted 1573.

entries.author: Dante Alighieri
entries.index: De Monarchia banned at Trent 1554; placed on Roman Index 1559; remained until 1881.

entries.author: Lorenzo Valla
works: De falso credita et ementita Constantini donatione
entries.index: Donation of Constantine treatise on Roman 1559.

entries.author: Jan Hus
entries.index: Roman 1559; condemned at Council of Constance 1415, burned 6 Jul 1415.

entries.author: John Wycliffe
entries.index: Roman 1559; works also burned posthumously per Council of Constance 1415; remains exhumed and burned 1428.

entries.author: Jean Bodin
works: De la République (Six livres de la République)
entries.index: République on Roman Index 1592; Démonomanie corrected; Heptaplomeres unpublished in his lifetime due to its religious heterodoxy.
entries.notes: Heptaplomeres (dialogue between adherents of seven religions) circulated only in manuscript until 1857.

entries.author: Lucilio Vanini
entries.index: Roman 1616; burned at Toulouse 1619 with his books, tongue cut out before execution.
entries.notes: Naturalistic Aristotelian; one of the most spectacular executions for unbelief in the early modern period.

entries.author: Cesare Cremonini
entries.index: Various works on Roman Index from 1666.
entries.notes: Paduan Averroist; refused to look through Galileo's telescope.

entries.author: Bernardino Telesio
works: De rerum natura iuxta propria principia
entries.index: Roman 1596 donec corrigatur.
entries.notes: Naturalistic Renaissance philosopher; teacher of Campanella.

entries.author: Francesco Patrizi
entries.index: Nova de universis philosophia (with Hermetic and Chaldean Oracle texts) condemned 1594.
entries.notes: Edited the Hermetica; sought to replace Aristotle with a Hermetic-Neoplatonic curriculum.

entries.author: Pietro Aretino
entries.index: Roman 1559; nearly all works prohibited.

entries.author: Anton Francesco Doni
entries.index: Roman 1559.

entries.author: Bernardino Ochino
entries.index: Roman 1559.

entries.author: Pier Paolo Vergerio
entries.index: Roman 1549; ex-bishop turned Reformer.

entries.author: Jacob Boehme
entries.index: Aurora MS confiscated 1612 by Görlitz authorities under Gregor Richter; Boehme banned from writing 1612-1619. Works not on Roman Index (Protestant author) but suppressed by Lutheran consistories.
entries.notes: Suppressed by Lutheran orthodoxy rather than Rome.

entries.author: Caspar Schwenckfeld
entries.index: Schmalkaldic League 1540; Luther denounced; later on Roman Index.

entries.author: Valentin Weigel
entries.index: Suppressed by Lutheran orthodoxy; works printed posthumously 1609 onward.
entries.notes: Lutheran pastor; works circulated secretly until decades after his death.

entries.author: Johann Reuchlin
entries.index: Augenspiegel condemned by Leo X 1520 after the long Reuchlin-Pfefferkorn affair; the Kabbalistic works (De verbo mirifico, De arte cabalistica) suspected but not formally condemned.
entries.notes: First Christian Hebraist; defended the Talmud against Pfefferkorn's burning campaign.

entries.author: Talmud
entries.index: Roman 1559 (Paul IV); thousands of copies burned at Cremona 1559. Earlier Paris burning 1242, Pope Innocent IV. Sixtus V 1590 permitted expurgated edition.
entries.notes: Wholesale burnings: Paris 1242, Cremona 1559. The Basel Talmud (1578-81) heavily expurgated.

entries.author: Zohar
entries.index: Hebrew books generally suppressed under Paul IV 1559; later editions tolerated due to Christian Kabbalist interest. Knorr von Rosenroth's Kabbala Denudata (Latin translation, 1677-84) tolerated.

entries.author: Pseudo-Geber
entries.index: Latin alchemical corpus generally suspect under Roman Index; not always explicitly listed but circulation discouraged.

entries.author: Arnaldus de Villa Nova
entries.index: Some theological and alchemical works condemned 1316 (posthumously) and on Roman Index 1559.

entries.author: Cornelis Drebbel
entries.index: Drebbel's works circulated under Protestant patronage; not on Roman Index but suspect as alchemy.
entries.notes: Included for context; not formally banned.

entries.author: Michel de Montaigne
entries.index: Essais on Roman Index 1676.

entries.author: Pierre Charron
entries.index: Sagesse on Roman Index 1605.

entries.author: Marin Mersenne
entries.index: Mersenne attacked Fludd, Bruno, Cardano. Not banned; included for context.

entries.author: Gerolamo Cardano
entries.index: Tried by Inquisition 1570; works on Roman Index 1571.
entries.notes: Mathematician, physician, astrologer; cast the horoscope of Christ.

entries.author: Giovanni Battista della Porta
entries.index: Magia naturalis investigated by Inquisition; some editions corrected; physiognomic works on Index 1592.
entries.notes: Founder of Accademia dei Segreti, disbanded by Inquisition.

entries.author: Hermann von Wied
entries.index: Roman 1551.

entries.author: Sebastian Franck
entries.index: Roman 1559; spiritualist Reformer.

entries.author: Theophrastus von Hohenheim (pseudo-Paracelsiana)
entries.index: Theological pseudo-Paracelsian writings on Index.

entries.author: Conrad Gessner
entries.index: Roman 1559; Class I auctor damnatus because Protestant; later expurgated editions of natural-history works permitted.

entries.author: Olaus Magnus
entries.index: Roman 1559.

entries.author: Theodore Beza
entries.index: Roman 1559; Class I auctor damnatus.

entries.author: Philipp Melanchthon
entries.index: Roman 1559; Class I auctor damnatus.

entries.author: Hugo Grotius
works: Annotationes in Vetus et Novum Testamentum
entries.index: De jure belli on Roman Index 1626; theological works donec corrigantur.

entries.author: Samuel Pufendorf
entries.index: Roman Index 1701.

entries.author: John Toland
entries.index: Burned by Irish parliament 1697; pantheism term coined.

entries.author: Anthony Collins
entries.index: Roman Index 1713.

entries.author: Matthew Tindal
works: Christianity as Old as the Creation
entries.index: Roman Index 1734.

entries.author: Pierre Charron
entries.index: Roman 1605.

entries.author: Pomponius Algerius
entries.index: Executed by boiling in oil/lead, Rome 1556.

entries.author: Christoph Besold
entries.index: Suspect by Lutheran authorities; converted to Catholicism.

entries.author: Andreas Libavius
entries.index: Anti-Paracelsian; not banned but caught in Paracelsian controversies. Included for catalog cross-ref.

entries.author: Petrus Ramus
entries.index: Roman 1559 (Class I); killed in St Bartholomew's Day Massacre 1572.

entries.author: Caelio Secondo Curione
entries.index: Roman 1559.

entries.author: Olympia Fulvia Morata
entries.index: Roman 1559.

entries.author: Cornelius Loos
entries.index: Suppressed; printed sheets seized at Cologne 1592.
entries.notes: Critic of witch trials; suppressed before publication.

entries.author: Friedrich Spee
entries.index: Published anonymously 1631 due to censorship pressure; Jesuit author kept identity hidden.
entries.notes: Foundational critique of witch trials; not formally on Index but written under threat of suppression.

entries.author: Johann Weyer
entries.index: Roman Index 1571.
entries.notes: Demonologist who argued accused witches were mentally ill; Pseudomonarchia daemonum is the source for the Goetia hierarchy.

entries.author: Reginald Scot
entries.index: Ordered burned by James I 1603 (English suppression, not Roman Index).
entries.notes: Sceptical of witchcraft; preserved much grimoire material the author intended to debunk.

entries.author: Pseudo-Ficino / Pseudo-Albertus / grimoire tradition
entries.index: Not formally on Roman Index (circulated clandestinely in MS) but condemned wherever found. Picatrix in particular hunted by inquisitors.
entries.notes: The clandestine magical literature — never printed in their period, but extant in numerous MSS. Highest acquisition priority for an esoteric library.

entries.author: Cyrano de Bergerac
works: L'Autre Monde: Histoire comique des États et Empires de la Lune
entries.index: Manuscripts heavily censored at posthumous publication 1657; full text suppressed until 19c.

entries.author: Athanasius Kircher
entries.index: JESUIT — works generally approved, NOT banned. Included as negative-case to avoid false matches.

entries.author: Petrus Severinus
entries.index: Paracelsian; suspect but not formally on Index.

entries.author: Joseph Glanvill
entries.index: Not on Roman Index; included for esoteric-witchcraft context.

entries.author: Henry More
entries.index: Not on Roman Index but Cambridge Platonist works suspect in Catholic context.

entries.author: Anne Conway
works: The Principles of the Most Ancient and Modern Philosophy
entries.index: Not on Index but author of Kabbalistically-influenced philosophy with van Helmont.

entries.author: Francis Mercury van Helmont
entries.index: Tried by Inquisition 1661-1663; works circulated under Protestant patronage. Not formally on Index.

entries.author: Jean Baptiste van Helmont
entries.index: Father of FM van Helmont; works condemned by Louvain 1625; tried by Spanish Inquisition.

entries.author: Christian Knorr von Rosenroth
entries.index: Tolerated due to Christian Kabbalist framing; not on Roman Index.

entries.author: Edward Kelley
entries.index: Imprisoned by Rudolf II for failed transmutations; works (Theatrum astronomiae terrestris, etc.) suspect. Not formally on Index.

entries.author: John Dee
entries.index: Not formally on Roman Index. Dee's library burned by mob 1583; angelic conversations suppressed within Anglican context.
entries.notes: Included though not on Roman Index — Monas is canonical and his enochian-angelic MSS are the clearest case of self-censored esoteric work.

entries.author: Aleister Crowley
entries.index: Deported from France 1929; works variously suppressed but never on Roman Index (post-1900s, by which time the Index was moribund).

entries.author: Marie de Gournay
entries.index: Not banned; included for Montaigne-circle context.

entries.author: Tycho Brahe
entries.index: Not on Roman Index; Tychonic system explicitly approved by Jesuit astronomers as alternative to Copernicus.
